title: Have and Get Something Done
summary: Use have or get + object + past participle when someone arranges for another person to provide a service, with the object before the participle. Use the same have construction to describe an unwanted event affecting a person or their belongings, and distinguish it from doing the action yourself.
learningObjectives: Use have + object + past participle to describe services completed by someone else.
Maintain the correct object–participle order through questions, negatives and different tenses.
Use get + object + past participle as a natural alternative when arranging a service.
Interpret have something done as either an arranged service or an incident suffered, depending on context.

explanation.heading: Arrange a service rather than do it yourself
explanation.body: Have something done means that the subject arranges for someone else to perform an action. The subject may book and pay for the service without doing the work. This differs from a plain active sentence, where the subject performs the action. The person providing the service can be named with by when relevant but is often omitted.
explanation.example: Amelia had her bicycle repaired at the shop rather than repairing it herself.

explanation.heading: Keep the object before the past participle
explanation.body: The basic order is have + object + past participle: have the camera cleaned, not have cleaned the camera when the intended meaning is a service. The object may be a noun phrase or a pronoun. The final verb names the service and stays in its past-participle form even as the form of have changes.
explanation.example: They have the office windows washed twice a year.

explanation.heading: Change the tense of have to match the situation
explanation.body: Use have, has, had, will have, have had, or be having according to when the arrangement or service occurs. For questions, move the appropriate auxiliary before the subject: Did you have the locks changed? For a service in progress, use be having + object + participle. Never insert do/does in front of a main past participle.
explanation.example: We are having the conference room painted this week.

explanation.heading: Use get something done for an arranged service
explanation.body: Get + object + past participle is a common alternative to have + object + past participle in ordinary conversation, often stressing that the service will be completed. It takes normal tense forms: get, got, have got or will get. Keep the object before the participle in this pattern too.
explanation.example: I need to get my laptop screen replaced before Monday.

explanation.heading: Describe something that happened to someone
explanation.body: Have + object + past participle can also describe an event suffered by the subject, often an unpleasant one. Someone who had their wallet stolen did not arrange a theft. The context distinguishes experience from a deliberately arranged service. Avoid interpreting every had + object + participle as a paid request.
explanation.example: While travelling, the family had their luggage damaged in transit.

explanation.heading: Choose the meaning from the surrounding facts
explanation.body: A useful test is whether the subject booked a service or was affected by an unexpected event. Both sentences may have the same grammar, but the intention is different: having a parcel delivered is normally arranged; having it stolen is not. If the subject did the work, use a normal active verb instead.
explanation.example: After the storm, they had their broken fence repaired by a carpenter.

comparisons.title: Do it yourself versus arrange a service

left.label: Direct action
left.note: The subject personally performed the cleaning.

right.label: Arranged service
right.note: Someone else cleaned the sofa for Hugo.

comparisons.title: Have and get in service arrangements

left.label: Have something done
left.note: Have commonly states that someone performed a service for us.

right.label: Get something done
right.note: Get offers a conversational alternative with essentially the same service meaning.

left.label: Booked service
left.example: Lena had her front door replaced.
left.note: She arranged for the door to be replaced.

right.label: Unwanted event
right.example: Lena had her front door damaged.
right.note: The door was damaged; she did not necessarily arrange it.

examples.sentence: Mika has her car serviced at the same garage each spring.
examples.note: The service is regularly performed by a mechanic.

examples.sentence: Did you have your passport photograph taken yesterday?
examples.note: Did helps form a question; the object comes before taken.

examples.sentence: We are getting the meeting room decorated before the ceremony.
examples.note: Get + object + participle works in a continuous form.

examples.sentence: The café will have its sign repaired next week.
examples.note: Will have refers to arranging a future repair.

examples.sentence: The traveller had his phone stolen during a bus journey.
examples.note: Had his phone stolen means he experienced a theft.

examples.sentence: I had the curtains shortened to fit the new windows.
examples.note: The curtains were shortened by someone providing a service.

commonMistakes.incorrect: We had cleaned the carpets by a specialist yesterday.
commonMistakes.correct: We had the carpets cleaned by a specialist yesterday.
commonMistakes.why: For a service, put the object before the participle: had the carpets cleaned.

commonMistakes.incorrect: I am having painted my kitchen this week.
commonMistakes.correct: I am having my kitchen painted this week.
commonMistakes.why: The object my kitchen must come between having and painted.

commonMistakes.incorrect: She got her camera repair at the shop.
commonMistakes.correct: She got her camera repaired at the shop.
commonMistakes.why: Get something done requires a past participle, not the base form repair.

commonMistakes.incorrect: He had his backpack stealing on the train.
commonMistakes.correct: He had his backpack stolen on the train.
commonMistakes.why: Stolen is the past participle; the context describes an unwanted theft.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Did you had your jacket altered?
commonMistakes.correct: Did you have your jacket altered?
commonMistakes.why: After did, use the base form have before the object and participle.

studyTips: With a service sentence, identify three pieces in order: have/get, the object, and the past participle.
Contrast pairs aloud: I repaired my bike / I had my bike repaired, then say who actually performed the repair.
Ask whether the event was arranged or unwanted before interpreting had something done; surrounding details decide the meaning.

exercises.prompt: The team did not install the new lights themselves. They ___ by an electrician.
exercises.feedback: Had the lights installed puts the object between had and the past participle, showing an arranged service.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means that Mia arranged for a professional to clean her coat?
exercises.feedback: Had her coat cleaned says Mia arranged for somebody else to perform the service.

exercises.prompt: My passport photo is outdated. I need to ___ before applying.
exercises.feedback: Get a new photo taken is get + object + past participle.

exercises.prompt: During the burglary, Omar ___ while he was away. He did not arrange this.
exercises.feedback: Had his laptop stolen describes a theft that affected Omar, not a service he requested.

exercises.prompt: The landlord hired a painter to repaint the hall yesterday. The landlord ___ (have / the hall / repaint) yesterday. Use the causative past simple.
acceptedAnswers: had the hall repainted
exercises.feedback: Had the hall repainted means the landlord arranged the painting; the object precedes the participle.

exercises.prompt: An optician checks Eva’s eyes every year. Eva ___ (have / her eyes / check) every year. Use the present simple.
acceptedAnswers: has her eyes checked
exercises.feedback: A singular subject takes has, followed by her eyes and the participle checked.

exercises.prompt: The café has booked an engineer to fix its espresso machine next week. The café ___ (get / its espresso machine / fix) next week. Use be going to.
acceptedAnswers: is going to get its espresso machine fixed
exercises.feedback: Is going to get describes the planned service, with its espresso machine before fixed.

exercises.prompt: An airline damaged our luggage during a trip last month. We ___ (have / our luggage / damage) during the trip. Use have something done to describe an unwanted experience.
acceptedAnswers: had our luggage damaged
exercises.feedback: Had our luggage damaged describes what happened to us, not a service we requested.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: We had fixed the boiler by a technician yesterday.
acceptedAnswers: We had the boiler fixed by a technician yesterday.
exercises.feedback: To express an arranged repair, the boiler must appear before the participle fixed.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: I am having painted my living room this week.
acceptedAnswers: I am having my living room painted this week.
exercises.feedback: In the causative structure, the object belongs between having and painted.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: She got her bicycle repair at the shop.
acceptedAnswers: She got her bicycle repaired at the shop.
exercises.feedback: Get + object takes a past participle: repaired.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: They had their wallets stealing on the train.
acceptedAnswers: They had their wallets stolen on the train.
exercises.feedback: Stolen is the past participle used when the owners suffered a theft.

speakingExercises.prompt: Carmen paid a mechanic to service her scooter yesterday. Say one sentence beginning “Carmen”, using had + object + past participle, and ending “yesterday”.
acceptedAnswers: Carmen had her scooter serviced yesterday.
speakingExercises.feedback: Had her scooter serviced expresses a service completed by a mechanic.

speakingExercises.prompt: Ask someone where a shop printed their wedding photos. Start with “Where did you” and use the causative verb have in a complete question.
acceptedAnswers: Where did you have your wedding photos printed?
speakingExercises.feedback: Did you have + object + printed forms a causative past question.

speakingExercises.prompt: Ben has not yet paid a technician to repair his broken laptop, so it remains broken. Begin “Ben”, use a negative present-perfect causative with repaired, and end “yet”.
acceptedAnswers: Ben has not had his laptop repaired yet.
Ben hasn't had his laptop repaired yet.
speakingExercises.feedback: Has not had his laptop repaired indicates that the arranged repair has not occurred.

speakingExercises.prompt: Your windows need cleaning, and you plan to pay someone next week. Begin “We” and use be going to get + the windows + cleaned; end with “next week”.
acceptedAnswers: We are going to get the windows cleaned next week.
We're going to get the windows cleaned next week.
speakingExercises.feedback: Get the windows cleaned means arranging for another person to clean them.

speakingExercises.prompt: Jules assembled his table himself instead of paying someone. Begin “Jules”, use a negative past causative with have, and finish “because he did it himself”.
acceptedAnswers: Jules did not have the table assembled because he did it himself.
Jules didn't have the table assembled because he did it himself.
speakingExercises.feedback: The negative causative contrasts an unbooked service with Jules doing the work himself.

speakingExercises.prompt: A thief stole Nora’s bag yesterday. Nora did not arrange the theft. Begin “Nora”, use have + object + past participle to describe the experience, and end “yesterday”.
acceptedAnswers: Nora had her bag stolen yesterday.
speakingExercises.feedback: Had her bag stolen describes an unwanted incident affecting Nora.

speakingExercises.prompt: This morning Priya fixed her bicycle herself but paid someone to clean her car. Say exactly two sentences, first beginning “Priya” in the active past simple, then beginning “She” with had + object + past participle. Omit the time reference.
acceptedAnswers: Priya fixed her bicycle herself. She had her car cleaned.
speakingExercises.feedback: Fixed describes personal action; had her car cleaned describes an arranged service.

speakingExercises.prompt: A client asks if you will repair the office door yourself. You have booked a carpenter. Respond in one sentence beginning “I”, using going to have + object + past participle.
acceptedAnswers: I am going to have the office door repaired.
I'm going to have the office door repaired.
speakingExercises.feedback: Going to have the office door repaired says that another person will do the work.

listeningExercises.audioText: My sister isn't painting the flat herself. She's having it painted by a local decorator next week.
listeningExercises.prompt: Who will actually paint the flat?
choices: Nobody; the flat will not be painted.
listeningExercises.feedback: Having it painted by a decorator means that someone else performs the service.

listeningExercises.audioText: I had my eyesight checked in March, but I still need to get new glasses made.
listeningExercises.feedback: Had my eyesight checked describes a completed service; the glasses are still a future need.

listeningExercises.audioText: The hotel had its windows cleaned before the conference.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the four-word causative phrase immediately after “The hotel”.
acceptedAnswers: had its windows cleaned
listeningExercises.feedback: Had its windows cleaned follows have + object + past participle.

listeningExercises.audioText: During their trip, the couple had their camera stolen at a crowded market.
listeningExercises.prompt: How should the event be understood?
choices: They hired someone to sell the camera.
listeningExercises.feedback: Had their camera stolen expresses a harmful experience, not an arranged service.

listeningExercises.audioText: We were going to get the floor repaired, but the company cancelled our appointment.
listeningExercises.prompt: What can be concluded about the arranged repair?
choices: The floor was repaired on schedule.
The repair did not take place at that appointment.
The speakers repaired the floor themselves.
listeningExercises.feedback: The company cancelled the booking, so the planned service was not carried out at that appointment.

listeningExercises.audioText: The manager has the air-conditioning filters replaced every three months.
listeningExercises.prompt: What does the manager arrange regularly?
choices: A weekly inspection of the whole building.
A filter replacement four times a year.
listeningExercises.feedback: Every three months means four times a year; has the filters replaced indicates an arranged service.

listeningExercises.audioText: I'm getting my passport renewed at the city office tomorrow.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the four words immediately after “I’m”.
acceptedAnswers: getting my passport renewed
listeningExercises.feedback: Getting my passport renewed means arranging the renewal service.

listeningExercises.audioText: Theo had his phone stolen at the sports centre.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the four-word phrase immediately after “Theo”.
acceptedAnswers: had his phone stolen
listeningExercises.feedback: Had his phone stolen describes an unwanted event affecting Theo.
